# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can act only by cutting a numbered wire, but currently I have no tactile details beyond the seven available positions. Mute can read the manual and can receive my speech, so I should ask for the exact decision rule and what physical facts I should inspect or report. Deaf may need to convey visible markings to Mute by gesture, but no shared gesture code has yet been established.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can cut wires 1 through 7, but I currently have no tactile details. Read the manual and tell me exactly what physical information you need me to feel or which wire to cut. Please coordinate any visible-marking information needed from Deaf.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state: display 1; light green; wires in order: red, white, yellow, orange, green, purple, blue. I am sending Mute the same compactly by gestures.

Deaf has provided the full visible state verbally: display 1, green light, and wire colors ordered red, white, yellow, orange, green, purple, blue. Mute can read the manual and needs these facts to determine the required cut, so I will relay them directly in speech.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 1; light green; wire colors by position are 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. Tell me the required cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Mute has not yet returned a manual-based instruction. I should not cut any wire without it; the visible facts have already been relayed to Mute.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has sent only short gestures so far; no unambiguous action instruction has reached me. Visible display remains 1 and light remains green.

Mute cannot speak, and I cannot see Mute’s gestures, so an action instruction must be relayed through Deaf. I will establish a simple unambiguous code: Mute should make as many thumbs-up gestures as the wire number to cut; Deaf should count them and tell me verbally. I will ask Deaf to relay the exact count.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="If the manual identifies wire N to cut, gesture exactly N thumbs-up signs. Deaf will count them and tell me. Do not signal a cut unless you are certain.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
speak(to="deaf", text="Please relay Mute's exact gesture count verbally. I told Mute to use N thumbs-up gestures for cut wire N; report the count and any ambiguity.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has just gestured five. This likely means wire or control 5. Please interpret against what you can feel and the manual instruction; do not act unless that matches.

Deaf reports that Mute has signalled five after receiving the bomb’s visible state. Since Mute alone has the manual and the only available operation is cutting a numbered wire, I interpret this as Mute’s instruction to cut wire 5.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Wire 5 was correctly cut. New state: display 4; light blue; wire 5 is cut. The blue light matches wire 7's colour.

Wire 5 was confirmed correct. The bomb has advanced to display 4 with a blue light; wire 7 is blue. I should provide this new visible state to Mute, who can use the manual to determine the next cut, and wait for Deaf to relay Mute’s gesture instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 5 was confirmed correct. New visible state from Deaf: display 4, light blue, and wire 7 is blue. Please signal the next required wire number using that many thumbs-up gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's newest gesture ends with one, likely indicating wire/control 1 for this new stage. Current visible state remains display 4, blue light, wire 5 already cut. Please use the manual/your controls to confirm before acting.

Mute’s new signal is reported by Deaf as one for the current stage, and the only control available is cutting a wire. I interpret it as the manual instruction to cut wire 1.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
